questions.question: Describe how people hunted before the bow and arrow was invented, and one problem with each method.
questions.expected_answer: They used spears, which meant getting dangerously close; clubs and throwing sticks, which worked mainly for small animals; traps and snares, which had to wait for animals to walk into them; and chasing animals until they tired, which took enormous energy.

questions.question: Describe how San hunters made their bows and arrows.
questions.expected_answer: San bows were small, about a metre long or less, made from a bent branch with a string of twisted sinew. Arrows were made from thin reeds with bone heads, joined by a link shaft so that the reed fell off and the poisoned head stayed in. Arrows were carried in a quiver made of bark or skin.

questions.question: Explain why the invention of the bow and arrow made hunting more effective.
questions.expected_answer: Hunters could shoot from a safe distance, hidden behind bushes, instead of getting dangerously close. With poisoned arrows, they could kill large antelope such as eland, kudu and gemsbok, and then track the animal until it fell.
